title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck axiomatises a 'magasin' (M, ≤, ≪, |·|). This appears to be a combinatorial model of tame or polyhedral decompositions. ≤ is an order between pieces. X ≪ Y reads 'X refines Y'. |·| (written |∘| on the next page) is a symmetric, antireflexive disjointness relation. The tilde notation X̃ appears to be the set of elements ≤ X. The previous page noted that the 'immediate refinement' relation ∘≪, together with ≤, recovers ≪ by (*): X ≪ Y ⇔ ∃Y' with X ∘≪ Y' ≤ Y. This page asks the converse question. Given a datum (M, ≤, ∘≪, |·|), when does (a) defining ≪ by (*) give a magasin, and (b) ∘≪ come out as exactly the immediate-refinement relation of that magasin?

Answer worked out on the page:
- (1) Assume ≤ and ∘≪ are partial orders.
- (2) Commutation/exchange axiom: X ≤ Y ∘≪ Z ⇒ ∃Z' with X ∘≪ Z' ≤ Z. In relational terms, (≤ ; ∘≪) ⊆ (∘≪ ; ≤).
- (2') Uniqueness: the middle term Y' in X ∘≪ Y' ≤ Y is unique.

With these, ≪ = (∘≪ ; ≤) is an order, which gives Mag 1:
- Reflexivity: X ∘≪ X ≤ X.
- Transitivity: from X ∘≪ Y' ≤ Y ∘≪ Z' ≤ Z, apply (2) to Y' ≤ Y ∘≪ Z' to get Y' ∘≪ Z'' ≤ Z', hence X ∘≪ Z'' ≤ Z.
- Antisymmetry: it reduces to X ≤ Y ∘≪ X. Then Y ∘≪ X ≤ Y and Y ∘≪ Y ≤ Y, so uniqueness forces X = Y.

Also, if X ∘≪ Y and X ≪ Y' ≤ Y, uniqueness forces Y' = Y. So ∘≪ is contained in immediate refinement, and conversely immediate refinement implies ∘≪.

The resulting axiom system:
- Mag 1': ≤ and ∘≪ are orders.
- Mag 2' a): the factorisation X ∘≪ Y' ≤ Y is unique.
- Mag 2' b): if X ∘≪ Y, then every X' ∈ X̃ has some Y' ∈ Ỹ with X' ∘≪ Y'. Reading X̃ as the down-set of X, this is exactly axiom (2), which is why (2) no longer appears separately.
- Mag 3', Mag 4': as before; per the margin, these link ∘≪ with |·| and ≤ with |·|.

Grothendieck remarks the system is neither simpler nor more complicated than Mag 1–4, but ∘≪ seems more 'primary'. The next page adds that ≤ and ∘≪ are 'disjoint', (X ≤ Y ∧ X ∘≪ Y) ⇔ X = Y, which also follows from uniqueness. In modern terms: two orders on one set with a distributive law, whose composite order carries a strict (unique) factorisation system.
errors: No mathematical error. The reduction of antisymmetry of ≪ to the uniqueness axiom (2') is left implicit but works, as shown above.

The page states that Mag 2 'becomes automatic' yet keeps Mag 2' b) in the summary. This is consistent only if Mag 2' b) is read as the reformulation of the exchange axiom (2) (taking X̃ as the down-set). That identification is not stated explicitly.

ideas.what: Recover the refinement order ≪ as the composite of the immediate-refinement order ∘≪ and the order ≤, and characterise when this composite is again an order with ∘≪ as its immediate part.
ideas.modern_name: Distributive law between two (pre)orders / composite of relations; strict factorization system on a poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Beck (distributive laws, 1969); Rosebrugh–Wood (distributive laws and factorization, 2002); Grandis (strict factorization systems)

ideas.what: Exchange axiom X ≤ Y ∘≪ Z ⇒ ∃! Z' with X ∘≪ Z' ≤ Z, with uniqueness of the middle term.
ideas.modern_name: Unique factorization (orthogonal/strict factorization system) in a poset category

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'magasin' with order, refinement and disjointness relations as a combinatorial foundation for tame topology / analysis situs.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial models of stratified/polyhedral decompositions (cf. o-minimal cell decompositions, face posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Unsure; tame topology programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)
ideas.where_published: Only the general tame-topology programme appears in the Esquisse; the magasin axioms are unpublished.

missed.claim: The 'magasin' axiomatics (Mag 1'–4') as a purely order-theoretic foundation of tame topology was never developed or published. The page shows a clean reformulation in terms of two orders with a unique-factorisation law plus a disjointness relation. Whether this structure actually models polyhedral or o-minimal decompositions was never tested in the literature.
missed.quote: Ce n'est pas plus simple ni moins simple que Mag 1 – Mag 4, mais le domaine de ∘≪ paraît plus "primaire"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly of historical interest. It could be compared with face-poset and stratification-poset approaches to tame/o-minimal topology, but the mathematics on this page is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary order theory: a distributive law between two orders giving a composite order with unique factorisation. Its interest is as an unpublished step in Grothendieck's tame-topology 'magasin' axiomatics, not as a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'la relation en [?] défaut [?] ∘≪' is probably 'la relation de départ ∘≪' (the given relation ∘≪).
In (1), the relations listed are '≤, ∘≪' with a struck-out word replaced by an insertion; read as '≤, ∘≪ [sont des] relations d'ordre'.
In the paragraph 'Sous ces conditions…', the struck symbol is X; the conclusion reads 'i.e. X est raffinement immédiat de Y'.
The left-margin words 'cond 5' and 'Artinien' are uncertain readings and may be different words.
